sources.title: Joachim Kock, Frobenius algebras and 2D topological quantum field theories (short version)
sources.locator: §§1.3.5–1.3.20 and 3.1.12–3.1.13 (PDF pp. 14–20, 34–36); §2.4 (PDF pp. 26–30) for the inverse-pairing coproduct.
sources.reading_extent: Downloaded and inspected the complete 48-page short-version PDF. Read the complete surface classification/normal-form and generator-relation argument on pp. 14–20, the finite-dimensional Frobenius/comultiplication reasoning on pp. 26–30, and the closed TQFT/Frobenius category correspondence on pp. 34–36. The author explicitly identifies this document as a condensed short version of larger minicourse notes.

contents.name: §1.3.5–1.3.20: closed connected surfaces, genus normal form, elementary sewing relations and reduction

source_review.read_extent: Read the definition of genus, connected-surface normal form, generator relations, and finite reduction to genus handles.
source_review.supports: Supports the handle/cup/cap sewing route. It does not compute the particular weights w_i or prove reflection positivity; those finite calculations are local.

contents.name: §2.2 and §2.4: Frobenius forms and the induced counital comultiplication

source_review.read_extent: Read the nondegenerate Frobenius-form convention, construction of the coproduct from the inverse pairing, counit, Frobenius identities, and coassociativity proof.
source_review.supports: Supports identifying Δ as the inverse-pairing coproduct and checking the structure maps. The explicit diagonal-weight calculation remains local.

contents.name: §3.1.12–3.1.13: closed 2D TQFTs and commutative Frobenius algebras

source_review.read_extent: Read the closed cobordism generators, their Frobenius equations, functor construction, and the induced equivalence on objects and morphisms.
source_review.supports: Supports the closed-sector classification used for the model. No open sector, Cardy data, positivity condition, or fully extended point-level result is claimed.

contents.name: §3.1.12–3.1.13: arbitrary commutative Frobenius algebras give closed TQFTs

source_review.read_extent: Read the converse construction from commutative Frobenius data to a symmetric monoidal functor.
source_review.supports: Supports applying the closed classification after the dual-number Frobenius structure is verified locally. It does not supply the dual-number matrix or nilpotent calculation.

contents.name: §3.1.12–3.1.13: no reflection-positivity hypothesis in the algebraic classification

source_review.read_extent: Read the classification hypotheses and the separate target symmetry convention.
source_review.supports: Shows only the algebraic classification boundary; the Hermitian form and positivity criterion are proved directly in the item.

sources.title: Joachim Kock, Frobenius Algebras and 2D Topological Quantum Field Theories (Cambridge book excerpt)
sources.locator: Retrieved Cambridge excerpt, PDF pp. 1–7, especially the closed cobordism/TQFT description and the Frobenius classification discussion on pp. 2–6.
sources.reading_extent: Downloaded the complete 10-page Cambridge University Press excerpt and read the relevant body on pp. 1–7: closed TQFT definition, closed cobordism objects and gluing, the surface generators, and the Frobenius classification/proof sketch. The later excerpt pages were checked for scope and contain front matter/contents rather than additional sewing arguments.

contents.name: Excerpt pp. 2–4: closed cobordisms, gluing, disjoint union, and the basic algebraic operations

source_review.read_extent: Read the closed category and the elementary surface-generator correspondence.
source_review.supports: Supports the exact no-free-boundary convention and the closed cobordism language. It is a book excerpt and a proof sketch, not the full book proof.

contents.name: Excerpt pp. 5–6: Frobenius equations and the 2D TQFT/Frobenius classification

source_review.read_extent: Read the classification statement and the construction in both directions as presented in the excerpt.
source_review.supports: Supports the closed-sector model; it does not give the diagonal-weight sum, dual-number calculations, or positivity argument.

contents.name: Excerpt pp. 5–6: closed surface generators yield the algebraic sewing relations

source_review.read_extent: Read the mapping from unit, multiplication, counit and comultiplication generators to Frobenius structure maps.
source_review.supports: Supports the topological meaning of H=μΔ; explicit amplitudes are calculated locally.

contents.name: Excerpt pp. 5–6: classification permits commutative Frobenius algebras without a positivity condition

source_review.supports: No reflection form or Hilbert positivity condition is asserted; positivity is checked locally.

contents.name: Excerpt pp. 5–6: a commutative Frobenius algebra supplies a closed TQFT

source_review.read_extent: Read the converse construction in the closed category.
source_review.supports: Supports the categorical implication after the example’s Frobenius axioms are verified locally.

sources.title: Aaron D. Lauda and Hendryk Pfeiffer, Open-closed strings: Two-dimensional extended TQFTs and Frobenius algebras, arXiv:math/0510664v3
sources.locator: §§3.3–3.7 (PDF pp. 18–39) for generators, relations and normal form; §4 (PDF pp. 39–42), especially Definition 4.4 and Corollary 4.6, for the closed sector.
sources.reading_extent: The complete 47-page v3 PDF was downloaded and inspected. Read the generator/relations and normal-form proof in §§3.3–3.7, including its termination measures; read §4’s functor construction, monoidal-equivalence proof, closed-subcategory definition, and Corollary 4.6. The article treats the larger open-closed category; the batch claims only the no-free-boundary closed sector.

contents.name: §§3.3–3.7: open-closed generators, relations and normal form

source_review.read_extent: Read the generators, boundary-relative move setup, and the finite normal-form reduction.
source_review.supports: The article’s source category includes intervals and colored free boundary; only its closed subcategory is used here. Its diagrammatic moves are source context, not premises of the local algebra proofs.

contents.name: §4, Definition 4.4 and Corollary 4.6: closed TQFTs are commutative Frobenius algebras

source_review.read_extent: Read the proof of the open-closed equivalence and the restriction to the closed subcategory leading to Corollary 4.6.
source_review.supports: Independently supports the closed classification. It does not assert that an open algebra equals a center, nor any point-level or positivity claim.

contents.name: §4, Corollary 4.6: closed-sector Frobenius data define a TQFT

source_review.read_extent: Read the closed-sector corollary and its dependence on the symmetric monoidal category equivalence.
source_review.supports: Supports applying the closed classification after the local dual-number axioms are verified; the numerical pairing and radical calculations are local.

contents.name: §4, Corollary 4.6: classification hypothesis has no positivity condition

source_review.read_extent: Read the closed-sector classification statement and its algebraic hypotheses.
source_review.supports: The article does not supply a reflection-positive form or Hilbert structure; the weight criterion is proved locally.

contents.name: §3.3–3.7 and §4: handles and closed Frobenius sewing maps

source_review.read_extent: Read the decomposition into elementary generators and the closed-sector functor evaluation route.
source_review.supports: Supports the use of the closed sewing convention; the diagonal handle eigenvalue and genus sum are calculated locally.
